newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 rebounds after cbank lets crown fall.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 rebounds after cbank lets crown fall.

text.p: Czech shares rose strongly at Tuesday's fixing on the Prague bourse as a wave of short term bullish sentiment swept the market after the central bank gave in to speculative pressure for a weaker crown, dealers said.
"Basically there was like a bubble of interest, the prices went up but I think that there won't be much follow through," said Jan Sykora of Wood and Company.

Sykora said that higher interest rates, the discount rate was raised to 13 percent from 10.5, would hurt many companies and that some markets in the region, such as Ukraine, would remain cheaper than Prague even after the crown's fall.
Major issues and some export oriented stocks posted strong gains -- most rising by around three percent.

SPT Telecom rose 87 crowns, 3.0 percent, to 2,987. Power utility CEZ gained 27 crowns, 2.9 percent, to 932 and Komercni Banka rose 54 crowns, 2.9 percent, to 1,864. The three shares taken together account for 45 percent of the PX50 index's capitalisation.
Skoda Plzen, a major Czech exporter, rose 28 crowns, 2.9 percent, to 962.
